claims: The Artemis II mission returned to Earth on April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II mission had a safe splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
The Artemis II mission splashed down at 8:07 p.m. EDT.
The Artemis II mission had a four-person crew consisting of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The crew of the Artemis II mission completed a 10-day mission.
The crew of the Artemis II mission became the first humans to journey around the moon in over 50 years.
The Orion spacecraft entered Earth's atmosphere at approximately 25,000 mph (40,000 km/h).
The Orion spacecraft hit the atmosphere at roughly 75 miles above the Pacific Ocean.
The Orion spacecraft experienced temperatures around 5,000°F on its heat shield.
The USS John P. Murtha recovered the crew and capsule.
Officials had some prior concerns regarding heat shield wear.
The re-entry and splashdown of the Artemis II mission were successful.
The crew of the Artemis II mission is undergoing post-mission medical evaluations.
